recipes.name: Grilled Apple and Swiss Cheese Sandwich
ingredients_raw: 0.5 medium Granny Smith apple - peeled, cored and thinly sliced

steps.text: Preheat a skillet over medium heat.

Lightly brush oil onto one side of each bread slice. Place one slice, oil-side down, into the preheated skillet. Arrange apple slices over bread, then top with Swiss cheese and remaining bread slice, oiled-side up. Cook until bread is golden brown and cheese is melted, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Apple and Swiss Cheese Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: Add an apple to your grilled cheese sandwich! My mother taught me this recipe, and it has become one of my favorite meals.

review.reviewBody: this is really good, i have made this before, but if you can find an onion bread, and use brie cheese and cook this as a grilled cheese its awsome!

I add Apple to my grilled cheese sandwiches but like to first soften the apple slices a bit by frying them in a bit of butter or oil. Try adding a little more Of a salty flavour by adding a slice of prosciutto.

I used deli sliced Swiss cheese and Granny Smith apple slices. I also used Nature’s Own small loaf Sourdough and Country Crock Plant Butter with Avocado Oil spread. I kept the heat low under the skillet to melt the cheese slice without burning the bread. It came out perfect. I would make this again.

This was a tasty but something was missing and with Swiss I tend to get that at times. For my 'food lovin' palate', Swiss Cheese is a bit too tough and while I like Swiss on somethings (like a nice big, thick Corned Beef Rueben on Rye umm..with Russian dressing and Sauerk)...oh wait...where was I??? Oh!...this sandwich...(ummmm...Ruuueeeben) ok..ok...um...Swiss doesn't really yield much flavor to me with this sandwich. I did however, give 'meself' 4 stars because the second time I used Harvarti Cheese instead. I like the buttery taste of the cheese better with the apples. I love and used Cameo--a little sweeter but still firm. I also butter my bread (100% Whole Grain--nutty flavor/crunchy toasted texture) with "Smart Balance" (omitted olive oil), sprinkled buttered sides with a bit of cinnamon/sugar, put one slice bread *butter sides down* on heated non-stick, put 1 slice of Harvarti down, my thin sliced apple, 1 more slice of Harvarti and then my other slice of bread. Pre-sliced Harvarti is usally thin. Using a wide-wide 'panny-cake' turner i.e spatula--I smashed ever-so gently. Just to help it a long a bit. Yeeuummie. If you try this...don't overdue it on the cinnamon/sugar or you will increase the chance of burning it in spots. Don't have flames or electric too high. Slow toasting is always better even with a 'Classic Grilled Cheese'. SLOWWW TOOOAST. I would have gave myself 5 but mine is a littttttlllle bit more fattening....;o)...but sometimes fat RULES.!!!

I used homemade sourdough bread and a Granny Smith apple. The apple flavor doesn't come through very much, and I put a fair bit in the sandwich. It's a nice filling sandwich nevertheless. I cooked it on a sandwich maker to get the grill lines. The added advantage of using the grill is that I could set a lower heat that would allow better cooking of the apple. I might try a bit of apple jelly with the apple next time and I might look for a stronger tasting apple.

My childhood best friend's mom introduced me to this YEARS back... this was one of our favorite after-school snacks! However, this version was lacking flavor in some ways. First, granny smith apples are too tart for this, in my taste. I usually use Fuji or Gala apples. Instead of making it a "sandwich", I take and toast each slice of bread. After toasting, spread a layer of mayo over each slice of bread, top with apples, then cover apples with sliced cheese (I always use Colby jack or cheddar... but swiss works well, too!). Place both slices on baking sheet & broil until cheese has melted. From there, you can either place slices together to create a sandwich, or simply eat each slice on it's own. 
Great, easy recipe... but definitely needs some sort of condiment!! (I found this version quite 'dry' and too plain in some ways.)I did not like the olive oil, when I tried this version. Maybe some butter would be better... but I really prefer the version I grew up with, using mayo & toasting/broiling instead of treating it like a grilled cheese.

This sounded so unusual that I had to try it. I don't know how this works, but wow, it does. I used rye bread(had on hand), shredded Jarlsberg Swiss, and a Pipin apple. I also added a few bacon bits. I coated my bread with mayo as my momma taught me to do. Simple, filling, and SO tasty. I think the key is to slice the apples thin as recipe stated. I also layered cheese, apples, then again cheese. My husband even raved about it even tho shocked at the ingredients! Definitely adding this to our regulars. Yum
It was good but better after I fried the apple slices a little and added some cinnamon.
Excellent blend. Try a different twist by adding smoked turkey and coat each side of the bread with lite whipped butter

Something a little different from the standard grilled cheese. I only had Swiss slices on hand, and they didn't seem to melt very well, so maybe shredded cheese would melt better? Because many reviewers mentioned it being bland, I put a little Dijon mustard inside of each slice and added a few pieces of bacon.
This recipe is even better if you add a very thinly sliced red onion to it! I like to put mine in a waffle-maker to cook, too! Kids love the pattern it makes on the outside of the bread.

I have to say up front, I used a Gala apple instead of Granny Smith. The Gala did not keep its crispness, but maybe a Granny Smith would. I wasn’t crazy about the Gala’s texture. I also think a little mustard would have given the sandwich a flavor boost. May try again with the correct apple and some mustard! I used seed bread as suggested which helped give the sandwich some structure. Overall, this is a nice Autumn lunch!
I wanted to see if it was possible to make a cheese and apple sandwich and it is so I'll be trying it out.
Surprisingly tasty. I would recommend slicing the apples very thin, otherwise it cancels out the taste of cheese.
A really nice alternative to the standard version
Add some ham or turkey to this, and use a spicy mustard.
It turned out very good! We will eat them again.
I'm not a big fan of green apples, but this isn't bad. And very easy to make.

I made it with the apples I had, Red delicious; which turned out a little sweet, especially when heated and the sugars come out. I will use granny smith next time. I used a sourdough bread; which was nice and crusty. Recipe was really good, especially with gooey Swiss cheese. Thank you!
Tasted great but apples kept sliding out of the sandwich, cook apples in butter to soften a bit first
